(i) a novel class of substituted aromatic heterocycles was identified as potential selective anti-leukemia agents, (ii) the most potent compounds (1, 2, 7) induced cell death by caspase-3/7 activation and (iii) the compounds demonstrated selective cytotoxicity against leukemic cell lines and solid tumors with low cytotoxicity against normal cells.
we identified several substituted aromatic five-member heterocyclic compounds with significant anti-leukemic properties against multiple pediatric leukemia subtypes.
we identified a small-molecule class with potential for the development of novel antileukemia agents.

the identification of novel small molecule scaffolds that induce cell death in leukemic cells, but not in normal cells.
the identification of substituted 5 membered-ring heterocyclic compounds with potent anti-leukemic activities.
the identification of small molecules that induce apoptosis in leukemic cells.

the identified compounds represent potentially new and selective antileukemic agents.
